### Ticket Type

🐛 Bug Report (Something isn't working)

### Environment & System Info

```Shell
OS: Windows 11 25H2 (Build 26200.9457)
- Python: 3.12.16
- LeRobot: 0.6.1
- OpenCV: 4.13.0
- FFmpeg: 9.0.2
- CPU: AMD Ryzen 7 8845H
- GPU: AMD Radeon 780M (No NVIDIA GPU)
```

### Description

## Description

I am experiencing unstable concurrent video capture when using two USB UVC cameras on Windows 11 with LeRobot 0.6.1.

Both cameras work normally when used individually, achieving approximately 30 FPS. However, when attempting to capture from both cameras simultaneously, one camera's frame rate drops dramatically to approximately 1 FPS, while the other continues operating at around 30 FPS.

In some tests, FFmpeg also reports I/O errors, causing one of the cameras to stop delivering frames.

I would like to determine whether this is related to LeRobot's camera management, OpenCV/DirectShow, Windows UVC drivers, or USB controller bandwidth and resource allocation.
## Hardware

I am using two USB UVC cameras:

| Camera | Resolution | USB Connection |
|---|---|---|
| 2K USB Camera | 2560 × 1440 | USB 2.0 High-Speed |
| USB Camera | 1920 × 1080 | USB 2.0 High-Speed |

Both cameras are currently connected to the same USB Root Hub.
One of the cameras is a Hikvision 2K USB Camera.

## Problem Description

When using either camera individually, video capture works normally at approximately 30 FPS.

However, when attempting to capture from both cameras simultaneously, the following behavior occurs:

- One camera continues operating at approximately 30 FPS.
- The other camera drops to approximately 1 FPS.
- The issue persists when changing the initialization order of the capture threads.
- In some configurations, FFmpeg reports I/O errors and stops receiving frames from one camera.

Importantly, I can reproduce the problem using standalone OpenCV and FFmpeg scripts, without involving LeRobot.

This suggests that the issue may exist at a lower level of the Windows camera capture stack, although this has not yet been conclusively determined.

## Tests and Observations

### 1. Single-camera Capture

Both cameras work normally when tested individually.

- OpenCV DirectShow backend: approximately 30 FPS for both cameras.
- LeRobot OpenCVCamera: the 2560 × 1440 camera can continuously capture for 10 seconds at approximately 30 FPS.

### 2. Concurrent Capture Using OpenCV

I created two independent `VideoCapture` instances and used separate threads to capture frames from both cameras simultaneously.

However, one camera's frame rate drops to approximately 1 FPS, while the other maintains approximately 30 FPS.

Changing the initialization order of the two threads does not resolve the issue.

### 3. Video Format Negotiation

I attempted to request MJPEG using OpenCV's `CAP_PROP_FOURCC`.

However, the actual reported video format remains YUY2.

When enumerating the available DirectShow video formats using FFmpeg, both cameras currently expose YUY2 and NV12 modes. No MJPEG mode is listed.

### 4. NV12 Testing

Both cameras can capture video independently using NV12.

However, simultaneous capture through FFmpeg DirectShow still results in dropped frames or I/O errors.

### 5. Buffer Testing

Increasing FFmpeg's `rtbufsize` can eliminate the "real-time buffer too full" warning in some tests.

However, this does not resolve the underlying concurrent capture failure.

## Questions

I would appreciate clarification on the following points:

1. Does LeRobot 0.6.1 officially support simultaneous capture from multiple `OpenCVCamera` instances on Windows?

2. Is there a recommended configuration for using multiple `OpenCVCamera` instances simultaneously on Windows, particularly regarding camera initialization, threading, and capture settings?

3. Does LeRobot provide or recommend alternative camera backends suitable for capturing from multiple UVC cameras on Windows?

4. Are there known limitations or compatibility issues involving OpenCV's DirectShow backend and multiple UVC cameras on Windows?

5. What would be the recommended approach to determine whether this issue originates from LeRobot, OpenCV/DirectShow, Windows UVC drivers, or USB controller bandwidth and resource allocation?

## Related Issues

I found several existing discussions that appear to be related:

- [#2754 – Multiple Innomaker cameras](https://github.com/huggingface/lerobot/issues/2754)
- [#3621 – Windows OpenCV camera configuration](https://github.com/huggingface/lerobot/issues/3621)
- [#1368 – OpenCV camera connection issues on Windows](https://github.com/huggingface/lerobot/issues/1368)
- [#717 – GStreamer error with multiple cameras](https://github.com/huggingface/lerobot/issues/717)

My setup appears particularly similar to #2754, especially regarding multiple USB cameras sharing the same USB controller.

However, my observed failure pattern is somewhat different: one camera drops to approximately 1 FPS while the other continues operating at approximately 30 FPS.

## Expected Behavior

Both USB cameras should be able to capture video simultaneously at their configured frame rates, ideally maintaining approximately 30 FPS without significant frame drops or I/O errors.

## Actual Behavior

One camera maintains approximately 30 FPS, while the other drops to approximately 1 FPS or stops delivering frames.

## Additional Information

I understand that this issue may be related to Windows camera drivers or USB controller limitations rather than being a bug in LeRobot itself.

I have already tested multiple capture configurations and formats, but have not yet identified the exact cause.

Any suggestions, troubleshooting advice, or working configurations would be greatly appreciated.

My immediate goal is to achieve stable simultaneous video capture from two USB cameras on Windows using LeRobot.

Thank you for your time and help!
